title: Elastic preemptive microbatch + kernel-priority shim to smooth embedding tail latency
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Embedding endpoint exhibits high tail latency (p99 spikes) under mixed-traffic patterns where small low-cost requests are delayed by infrequent long-context or large-batch work. This impacts interactive UX and downstream reranking SLAs.

Proposal: Build an elastic "shim" layer in the inference scheduler that performs two coordinated actions: (1) preemptive microbatch shaping — detect and break/reshape oversized in-flight microbatches that are blocking the fast-path and opportunistically drain a prioritized short-window for latency-sensitive requests, and (2) kernel-priority routing — surface lightweight kernel affinity hints (quantized vs float, cached-KV hotpath) to prioritize quick kernels on available GPUs. The shim sits between ingress and the kernel dispatcher and is designed to be low-risk and reversible.

Success metrics: reduce embedding endpoint p99 by >= 30% under the mixed synthetic workload (90% small single-vector requests, 10% large-context or batched requests) and p95 by >= 15% while keeping average throughput loss <= 3% and CPU overhead for scheduler < 2% of a node.

Scope: runtime scheduler + microbatch allocator + small changes to kernel dispatcher to accept a 2-bit priority hint. No model changes. Backwards compatible: when shim disabled, behavior reverts to current scheduler.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Preemption may increase overall throughput variance; plan favors tail reduction for latency-sensitive customers over peak throughput.
- Aggressive breaking of microbatches can reduce batching efficiency and increase token-cost; we will tune hysteresis to limit cost impact.
- Kernel-priority hints are advisory only; hardware-level contention still possible.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmarked reduction in p99 and p95 on unit perf cluster (perf-red-team harness) with recorded traces.
- Canary rollout to 10% of production traffic with realtime dashboards showing per-tenant p99, throughput, and cost impact.
- Unit and integration tests for preemption invariants (no request duplication, KV-cache correctness).

Rollout plan: prototype -> internal perf run -> review -> gradual canary (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Rollout guardrails: automated alarms if p50 increases by >10% or throughput drops by >5% or cost-per-inference increases by >4%.
